label: i-MO 210 Dual 4G/LTE-A router kit
description: i-MO IMO-210-2x4G-KIT - dual-modem 4G/LTE-A CAT6 bonding router kit for small branches and mobile sites: 2x Gigabit Ethernet (max 1 WAN), two internal CAT6 modems with up to four SIMs and A/B switching, 802.11ac access point, 2x USB 2.0, IPsec VPN, stateful firewall with WAN/DMZ/LAN zones, 12 V DC (external 110-220 VAC adapter), 20 W, -20 to +60 C. Bonded throughput > 150 Mbps.
notes: The port row is precise and small: '**LAN / WAN Interface 2 x Gigabit Ethernet (Max 1 x WAN)**' - two sockets, only one of which may be a WAN at a time, plus '2 x USB 2.0' which are not network interfaces. So `eth1` is declared WAN and `eth2` LAN: the parenthetical says the *pair* can supply at most one WAN, and which of the two takes that role is a configuration choice, not a hardware one. **Cellular is fitted, not optional, in this kit:** 'Cellular Data Connectivity: 2 x 4G/LTE - A CAT6 Modems', 'Cellular Data SIMS: up to 4' (2 SIMs per modem with A/B switching). The 2 modems are therefore declared as `wwan` ports with `role: "wan"` - the same shape the Peplink BR1 pair uses - because a bonding router that cannot be cabled to a cellular link cannot be tested. **CAT6 is the 3GPP UE category, not a measured rate:** it is the modem class the page names, and its downlink ceiling is 300 Mbit/s, which is what `speed` carries; the page's own throughput figure is different again - 'Max Bonded Throughput: > 150 Mbps' across the bonded links. **The radio is 802.11ac and the page quotes no PHY rate**, so `867M` is the 2x2 802.11ac ceiling this catalogue uses for that class and not a quoted figure. '4 x SMA - 2 x Cellular/MiMo + 2 x WiFi' are antenna connectors. **A kit, but not a bundle in the sense this catalogue refuses:** the box is one appliance with two modems screwed into it, so the two modems *are* ports on this device; the antennas and the maintenance fee are the accessories.
